title: Mira and the Little Cloud-Kitten
markdown:
Nestled high in the Cloudneedle Mountains, where the air smelled like sweet pine needles and sunshine, lived a young witch named Mira. Her cottage was as round and cozy as a mushroom, chimney puffing cinnamon and magic. Hair the colour of moonlight. Eyes that sparkled like dew on a spiderweb. She loved her little home: shelves of pebbles like tiny bits of rainbow, jars of potions bubbling with soft light, an armchair as soft as a cloud and perfect for sinking into after a day of arranging. The windowsill was her favourite stage. Pebbles liked to be turned so their sparkliest face met the sun. Mira took this seriously, which is why she heard the mew at all.

One sunny afternoon, while she carefully arranged sparkling pebbles on a sun-drenched windowsill, she heard it: a tiny sad mew, so small it could have been a sigh from a daisy. “Hmm.” Brow crinkling, a tiny cloud over the sun. “That sounds like someone needs a bit of looking after. A very little someone.”

She peeked outside her round blue door, the kind that opened with a cheerful creak. Curled by a patch of bright bluebells that seemed to nod hello: a tiny fluffy kitten. Softest white, like a puff of cloud that had tumbled from the sky and decided to nap. Delicate pink ears twitching at every breeze. Wide innocent eyes the colour of warm milk. Another little mew, a question hanging.

A flutter in Mira’s tummy. Not scary. A what-now flutter, curiosity and a tiny bit of worry. Clearly lost, alone on the big wide mountain. “Oh, you poor little thing.” Gentle as a lullaby. She scooped it up. Instant snuggle, warm against her chest. A rumbling like a tiny motorboat: a purr.

“I shall call you Pip. For you are as precious and small as a tiny little seed, full of growing joy and happy surprises.” Pip nuzzled her cheek. Mira’s smile bloomed.

The sun dipped, mountain peaks rose and gold, a giant watercolor. Pip’s eyes, so wide and curious, began to droop. “We must find your home, Pip.” The mountain paths, lovely as they were, could be confusing after dark, and a lost kitten needed a warm bed and a loving family.

Pip nestled securely, she stepped onto the mossy path into whispering pines, tall, majestic, needles rustling like secrets. “It’s quite peaceful, isn’t it?” Pip yawned, tiny pink tongue, needle-sharp teeth. He stretched. Then his eyes lit. A dancing firefly, blinking like a tiny star on the ground.

He wriggled free, a quick light tumble onto moss. “Mew!” Playful energy. Pounce, white blur on green, chasing the winking firefly. “Whoa there, little cloud-hopper! Are you trying to catch the winking stars on the ground?” Too much fun to notice her worry. Pounce, wiggle, tumble — then he looked up, energy fading. He couldn’t see Mira’s familiar comforting shape. A little wobbly, a tiny boat on a big wide sea. A little sigh.

A soft light flickered through the trees. Not a firefly: a gentle warm glow, bobbing. From behind a giant leafy fern, Flicker the elf, ears a little wiggle-waggle of curiosity, tunic woven from moonbeams, a little lantern, warm friendly light. “Lost, little ones?” Tinkling bells on a winter breeze.

Mira hurried, heart lighter. Pip, having found his way back to her legs, trotted happily, no longer wobbly. “Oh, yes! Pip is lost, and I’m trying to find his family before it gets too dark. He’s a little cloud-kitten, you see.”

Flicker smiled with his whole face. “Ah, the Meadow of Whispers. That’s where the little cloud-kittens love to play and tumble. I can guide you, if you like. The moon is just rising, and it makes the path quite clear.”

So they went, lantern steady, deeper into the mountain, past pines that leaned together like gossiping aunts who had decided to be kind. Moon through branches, silvery patterns, a magical wonderland. Cool air: damp earth, sweet moss, night-blooming flowers unfurling to the moon as if they had been waiting for an audience. Pip nestled snug again, a happy little ball, tired now, safe and warm, one paw hooked in Mira’s sleeve as if to say the firefly chase was over. Flicker hummed a walking tune that was mostly lantern-swing.

A clearing, milky moonlight. The Meadow of Whispers: grass as soft as velvet, flowers glowing faint and warm, like captured fireflies. Among the blossoms, several other fluffy white kittens tumbling and pouncing, little clouds drifting.

A larger very fluffy cat, eyes like emeralds, looked up. “Mew!” Joy and recognition. Pip wriggled, leapt from Mira’s arms, landed softly, ran to join them. Happy meows, little chirps, lots of purring. He looked so happy, batting at siblings.

Warmth in Mira’s chest, like sunshine filling a cozy room. Also a little pang, a tiny wistful feeling. She had grown rather fond of the purrs and playful pounces. “Thank you, Flicker.” Voice a little wobbly.

“It is always a joy to help good hearts find their way.” Gentle, knowing. A nod. “The mountain paths are clear now. Your way home is easy, lit by the moon.”

Mira knelt. Pip was busy chasing a butterfly made of moonlight. She stroked his fur one last time. “Goodbye, Pip.” Affection. He nudged her hand, a silent thank you, then off, a blur of white, after brothers and sisters.

They walked back toward the cottage. Moonlight a gentle blanket. Flicker did not say that kindness always finds its way back. He only kept the lantern steady until her round blue door, then went his own moonbeam way.

Mira opened the door. Cinnamon and magic wrapped her like a hug she had not known she needed. She sat by the window, watching the moon climb, a happy sigh, and a little empty space on the armchair where a cloud-kitten might have sat, which she left empty on purpose, in case of mews. The pebbles on the sill still sparkled. One, she thought, looked a little like a pink ear. She did not move it.
